benchmark_impact.procedure: scripts/rescore_dir.py over backend/benchmark/snapshots, before and after the canonical sanitization. Same rules, same tool, only the evidence changed.
benchmark_impact.cause_of_the_single_change: tech.demo_content counts independent signals. One address carried two of them in its own content - a theme-vendor name in the local part and a placeholder domain. Replacing the address removes that signal, the finding drops one severity band, and smartkp.com.ua gains one point. This follows directly from the approved sanitization.
benchmark_impact.stored_expectations_updated: none required; no test asserts a count over the snapshots and no assertion reads the content of an address, cookie or key

stack.note: The integration suite creates and drops its own crawldy_test_<uuid> database; the owner's `seo` database was not used by the suite.

frontend.command: npx vitest run (after the production build)
frontend.note: Zero skips. The 23 previously skipped tests are gated by describe.skipIf(!BUILT) on .next/BUILD_ID, evaluated at collection, so the build must exist before vitest starts. They spawn a real `next start` on 127.0.0.1:3477 and assert the four security headers, each exactly once, plus the absence of X-Powered-By, across nine routes. The gate was not modified and no assertion was weakened; the wait for the server moved from inside the first test into beforeAll, because vitest's 5s default applied there while the helper budgets 60s for it.

backend.result: no issues found in 136 source files

remaining_skips.reason: Parametrized cases whose URL is not http/https. The extractor filters those schemes earlier, so the assertion does not apply. An in-test guard, unrelated to PostgreSQL and requiring no external credentials. Carried forward unchanged from CRAWLDY-FINAL-GREEN-CLOSURE-01.

end_to_end.what: One complete local recovery flow through the queue and the capture transport
steps: request from /forgot for a known and an unknown address - identical 202 and body
exactly one letter produced; the unknown address produced none
link read from the captured letter, not from the database
reset screen validated the link before asking for a password
mismatched confirmation refused; correct one accepted

Change password in the cabinet: wrong current refused, correct one revoked the session

credentials_and_tokens.token_column: token_hash varchar(64) - the schema has no column able to hold a clear-text token
credentials_and_tokens.access_log_evidence: GET /v1/auth/password/reset?token=*** - verified on the live stack after the AUTH-011 fix; zero occurrences of the probe token in the log

clean_database_bootstrap_proven.method: A disposable PostgreSQL 16 container created for this task only: --rm, a tmpfs data directory, no named volume, its own port 127.0.0.1:55433, and a password generated in memory. The owner's seoagent_pgdata volume was never named, mounted or touched. Redis logical database 1 was used so the owner's queue on database 0 was untouched.

bootstrap_data_created_by_the_migrations.note: Migration 0014 seeds the four plan definitions with their entitlement sets using ON CONFLICT, so a repeated run neither fails nor overwrites a changed set. Nothing is read from the database at startup: the API lifespan touches only logging and the rate limiter.

public_configuration_the_frontend_reads.note: Empty lists rather than an error. Commercial rows are owner decisions and were not exported; the pricing page renders without prices and checkout answers 503 checkout.unavailable instead of failing.

first_administrator.proof: On the clean stack: register through the product returned 201; GET /v1/admin/commerce/offers returned 403; after --role admin the same session returned 200. An unknown address is refused with exit 1 and creates no user.

clean_database_bootstrap_proven.teardown: The disposable container was removed; it had no volume, so nothing persisted.
